title: Declare runtime footprint and pin-exemption playbook for lightweight/open-model onboarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: We keep seeing submissions of small/open models (variants with sparse updates or delta weights) that claim to be drop-in compatible but at runtime either blow up memory, introduce unsupported ops, or degrade latency unpredictably. Current onboarding guidance focuses on semantic compatibility and soft-pinning, but lacks clear runtime footprint declarations and an operational playbook for granting temporary pin-exempt status (i.e., allow service without full pin) for low-risk models.

Goal: Clarify the PRD-level requirements and acceptance gating for: 1) a small, machine-readable 'runtime_footprint' declaration that model authors submit with open-model intake, and 2) a documented pin-exemption/playbook that PMs + runtime can apply when a model meets low-risk criteria (low memory, no new kernel ops, passes smoke evals). This ticket defines the requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and the short-term compensating controls needed until ingestion validation is implemented.

Scope (in):
- Define runtime_footprint schema v1 (memory_estimate_mb_per_8k, cpu_threads_hint, required_kernel_features, kv-cache-friendly boolean, max_tmp_storage_mb).
- Define explicit pin-exemption checklist and evidence bundle (smoke-evals, runtime profiler artifact, declared fallback mapping).
- UX surface in Catalog UI for showing footprint and exemption status + rationale.
- PM + Eng-run pilot onboarding flow for up to 5 community models.

Out of scope (for now):
- Automatic enforcement in ingestion pipeline (ENG owned).
- Quantization recommendations and model optimization guidance (separate Optimize epic).
acceptance_criteria: Schema: 'runtime_footprint' v1 documented (fields and allowed enums). Confluence PR created and linked.
Validation checklist: a reproducible set of smoke-evals (<=2000 prompts) that must pass >=95% exactness/latency guardrails to be eligible for exemption.
Runtime evidence: for pilot models, profiler traces (Dedicated 2xA100 baseline) show peak GPU memory <= declared memory_estimate_mb_per_8k * 1.25 and no blocked kernel ops flagged.
Fallback mapping: an automated map of compatible pinned variants for each exempted model is available and exercised in canary traffic tests (failover latency < 1.5x baseline).
UI: Catalog entry shows 'Declared runtime footprint' and a visible 'Pin-exempt (pilot)' badge with rationale. Design mock attached and sign-off from Jocelyn Park recorded.
Telemetry: telemetry events emitted for the pilot (ingest_attempt, exemption_granted, exemption_revoked) and dashboard created in Console-Observability (owner: Eng Infra).
Security: Security review sign-off from Priya Rao (security) with explicit acceptance of exemption controls recorded in comments and PRD.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Keeping a minimal schema reduces friction for community submitters but increases runtime uncertainty; we hedge by requiring profiler artifacts and a pilot. 2) Full ingestion validation is higher effort; pilot will run with manual gating and automated telemetry to surface regressions quickly.
